calc-limits-06: $x=0$ daalo: upar $1-\cos 0=0$, neeche $0$ — $0/0$ form. Neeche $x^2$ hai, to upar ka $x^2$ wala term dhoondhna hai.
$u^2=(4x)^2=16x^2$ — square poore $4x$ ka hoga, sirf $x$ ka nahi. Aur $\frac{1}{2}$ mat chhodo; ab $x^2$ se divide karo.
calc-limits-07: $x\to\infty$ par upar $(\ln x)^2$ aur neeche $x$ dono $\infty$ — $\infty/\infty$ form. Sawaal hai: kaun tez badhta hai?
L'Hôpital: upar ka derivative chain rule se $2\ln x\cdot\frac{1}{x}$, neeche ka $1$.
Pehle step ke baad $\frac{2\ln x}{x}$ — abhi bhi $\infty/\infty$, ek baar aur L'Hôpital lagao. Dhyan: $\infty/\infty$ ko 1 mat samjho.
calc-limits-08: $\tan 3x$ aur $\sin 3x$ dono $\approx 3x$ — first-order terms cancel ho jaate hain. Neeche $x^3$ hai, to dono ka $u^3$ term chahiye.
Difference: $\frac{u^3}{3}-\left(-\frac{u^3}{6}\right)$ — minus ke baad sign plus ho jaata hai. Phir $u^3=(3x)^3$ daalo, sirf $3x^3$ nahi.
calc-limits-09: Base $\frac{1+x}{1-x}\to1$ aur exponent $\frac1x\to\infty$ — ye $1^\infty$ form hai, seedha 1 nahi.
$f-1=\frac{2x}{1-x}$. Ab ise $g=\frac1x$ se multiply karke $x\to0$ lo. Trap: sirf $(1+x)^{1/x}\to e$ lekar neeche wala part bhool jaana.
calc-limits-10: Har option alag check karo. Pehle dekho kaun sa sach me $0/0$ hai — ek option me $x=0$ daalne par $0/0$ nahi aata.
$\frac{x+2}{2x+1}$ me $x=0$ seedha daalo — L'Hôpital tabhi lagta hai jab form $0/0$ ho. $\frac{\ln(1+2x)}{2x}$ me upar-neeche dono me $2x$ hai, cancel socho.
calc-one-sided-06: Sirf left-hand limit ($x\to4^-$) poocha hai. $|x-4|$ ka sign $x<4$ par kya hai, wahi decide karega.
$\frac{(x-4)(x+4)}{-(x-4)}$ me $(x-4)$ cancel karo, minus sign bacha rahega. Trap: $|x-4|$ ko $x-4$ likh dena — wo right side ka form hai.
calc-one-sided-07: $x\to2^-$ matlab $x$ thoda sa 2 se kam, jaise $1.999$. Floor ki value wahan kya hai, ye pehle socho.
$1\le x<2$ par $\lfloor x\rfloor=1$. $x^2$ continuous hai, to wo seedha $2^2$ ki taraf jaata hai.
Do alag cheezein: $x^2\to4$ aur $\lfloor x\rfloor\to1$. Trap: $\lfloor 2\rfloor=2$ use karna — left se aate waqt floor abhi 2 nahi hua.
calc-one-sided-08: Poora function $e^{1/x}$ par tika hai. $x\to0^-$ aur $x\to0^+$ par $1/x$ alag-alag direction me jaata hai.
Left side: $e^{1/x}=0$ daalo, $\frac{5+0}{1+0}$. Right side: $\frac{5e^{-1/x}+3}{e^{-1/x}+1}$ banao. Trap: sides swap mat karna — left wala pehle likhna hai.
calc-one-sided-09: Do floor ek saath: $\lfloor x\rfloor$ aur $\lfloor -x\rfloor$. Teen cheezein alag nikalo — left limit, right limit, aur $f(2)$.
Left ($x=1.99$): $\lfloor x\rfloor=1$, $-x=-1.99$. Right ($x=2.01$): $\lfloor x\rfloor=2$, $-x=-2.01$. Floor of negative number: neeche wala integer.
$\lfloor -1.99\rfloor=-2$ aur $\lfloor -2.01\rfloor=-3$ (minus side par neeche). Ab dono sums aur $f(2)=\lfloor2\rfloor+\lfloor-2\rfloor$ compare karo.
calc-one-sided-10: Teen pieces: $x<1$, $x=1$, $x>1$. Limit sirf paas ke pieces se aata hai; beech ka $f(1)=5$ continuity ke liye dekhna hai.
Left limit $=\lim_{x\to1^-}(x^2+1)$, right limit $=\lim_{x\to1^+}(3-x)$. Equal hon to limit exists.
Dono me $x=1$ daalo aur compare karo; phir us limit ko $f(1)=5$ se milao. Trap: $f(1)$ alag hai isliye limit nahi — ye galat logic hai.
calc-continuity-const-05: Continuity ke liye $k$ ko $x\to0$ wale limit ke barabar hona chahiye. $x=0$ par upar $\sqrt{16}-4=0$, neeche 0 — $0/0$.
Square root wala $0/0$: conjugate $\sqrt{x+16}+4$ se upar-neeche multiply karo. Upar $(x+16)-16$ banega.
Upar $x$ bachta hai jo neeche ke $x$ se cancel hota hai; neeche $\sqrt{x+16}+4$ rehta hai. Ab $x=0$ daalo — trap: $+4$ bhool jaana.
calc-continuity-const-06: Break point $x=2$ hai. Left piece $ax+1$ aur right piece $x^2-a$ dono me $a$ hai — dono side ka value barabar karna hai.
$a$ wale terms ek side, numbers doosri side — sign badalna mat bhoolo: $-a$ left me aakar $+a$ banega, $+1$ right me jaakar $-1$.
calc-continuity-const-07: Teen cheezein barabar: left limit, $f(0)=8$, right limit. Left piece $0/0$ hai, right piece seedha.
$1-\cos u\approx\frac{u^2}{2}$ with $u=ax$: left limit $=\frac{a^2}{2}$. Right limit $=b$.
$\frac{a^2}{2}=8$ se $a^2$ nikalo, phir root — condition $a>0$ dekho. Trap: $\frac12$ chhod dena ya $a$ ki jagah $a^2$ add kar dena.
calc-continuity-const-08: $x=2$ par neeche $x-2=0$. Agar upar 0 nahi hua to limit infinite hoga — isliye pehle $a$ isi condition se nikalta hai.
Condition: numerator at $x=2$: $4+2a+6=0$. Phir quadratic factor karo, $(x-2)$ cancel hoga, aur $b$ = bacha hua factor at $x=2$.
$a$ milne ke baad $x^2+ax+6$ ko $(x-2)(x-c)$ ke roop me likho, $c$ ka sign dhyan se. Trap: $b$ nikalna bhool jaana.
calc-continuity-const-09: $x=1$ par left piece $k^2x+2$ aur right piece $3kx$ — $k$ ki equation quadratic banegi, to ek se zyada $k$ ho sakte hain.
Quadratic factor karte waqt signs dhyan se — $(k+\cdot)$ vs $(k-\cdot)$. Shak ho to har option ko $k^2+2$ aur $3k$ dono me daal ke compare karo.
calc-continuity-const-10: $\sin\frac1x$ akela 0 ke paas oscillate karta hai, lekin yahan wo $x$ se multiply hai. Ye squeeze wala case hai.
Bound $|x|$ ka $x\to0$ par kya hota hai? Wahi product ka limit hai. Trap: $\frac{\sin x}{x}\to1$ se confuse karna — yahan sine ke andar $\frac1x$ hai.
calc-composition-06: $(g\circ f)(1)=g(f(1))$ — pehle andar wala $f$ lagta hai. Aur $(f\circ g)(1)=f(g(1))$ — pehle $g$.
$f(1)=2\cdot1+1$, phir use $g(u)=u^2-3$ me daalo. Doosre ke liye $g(1)=1-3$, phir $f$ me.
$f(1)=3$, $g(3)=9-3$. $g(1)=-2$, $f(-2)=2(-2)+1$. Trap: order ulta lena — andar wala function pehle chalta hai.
calc-composition-07: Bahar $e^{u}$ hai jo har jagah continuous hai, to limit andar le ja sakte ho. Asli kaam andar ka $\frac{1-\cos x}{x^2}$ hai.
Andar ka limit nikalke $e^{(\cdot)}$ me daalo. Trap: $1-\cos x\approx x^2$ likh dena (half bhool gaye) ya andar $x=0$ daal ke 0 maan lena.
calc-composition-08: $f$ me $u=0$ par jump hai. Isliye dekhna padega $g(x)=-x^2$ zero ki taraf kis side se aata hai.
$x\ne0$ ke liye $-x^2<0$, matlab $u$ hamesha negative side se 0 ke paas. To $f$ ka piece $u+1$ lagega. $h(0)=f(g(0))=f(0)$ alag se nikalo.
Limit ke liye $f(-x^2)=-x^2+1$ ka $x\to0$ lo; value ke liye $f(0)=0^2+3$. Trap: $f(\lim g)$ seedha lagana — $f$ wahan continuous nahi.
calc-composition-09: 2027 baar compose karna haath se nahi hoga — pattern dhoondho. $f(2)$, $f(f(2))$, ... kuch steps nikalo.
$f(2)=\frac{1}{1-2}=-1$. Ab $f(-1)$ aur uske baad wala value nikalo — dekho kitne steps baad 2 wapas aata hai (cycle length).
Cycle 3 ka hai, to 2027 ko 3 se divide karke remainder lo; utne steps hi effectively bachte hain. Trap: remainder galat lena ($3\cdot675=2025$).
calc-composition-10: Floor tabhi jump karta hai jab andar wala $x^2$ kisi integer ko cross kare. Har option me dekho $x^2$ wahan cross karta hai ya sirf touch.
$x\to0^-$ par bhi $x^2$ positive hai — $\lfloor x\rfloor$ jaisa behaviour mat lo. $\sqrt2$ ke left-right $x^2$ ki floor value compare karo.
calc-differentiability-06: $|\sin x|$: andar $\sin x$ zero par sign badalta hai ($x<0$ par negative). Absolute value aise point par corner bana sakta hai.
Pehle continuity check karo, phir left aur right derivative alag: $f'(0^\pm)=\lim_{h\to0^\pm}\frac{|\sin h|}{h}$.
$h>0$: $|\sin h|=\sin h$, ratio $\to1$. $h<0$: $|\sin h|=-\sin h$ — ab ratio ka limit nikalo aur compare karo. Trap: sirf right side dekhna.
calc-differentiability-07: Corner sirf $|x-2|$ se aa sakta hai. Dono sides par absolute value hata ke alag formula likho.
Right: $f'=2x-1$ at 2 $=3$. Left wala bhi isi tarah nikalo (minus sign ke saath), phir right minus left. Trap: order ulta karna.
calc-differentiability-08: $f(0)$ alag se 0 define kiya hai. Har option me teen alag cheezein hain: continuity, $f'(0)$ (definition se), aur $x\to0$ par $f'(x)$ ka behaviour.
$f'(0)=\lim_{h\to0}\frac{h^2\sin(1/h)-0}{h}=\lim h\sin\frac1h$. Aur $x\ne0$ par product + chain rule se $f'(x)$ nikalo.
$x\ne0$: $f'(x)=2x\sin\frac1x+x^2\cos\frac1x\cdot(-\frac1{x^2})$. Dekho kaunsa term 0 ki taraf nahi jaata. Trap: $f'(0)$ exist karna = $f'$ continuous maan lena.
calc-differentiability-09: Differentiable hone ke liye do conditions: values match (continuity) aur slopes match. Do unknowns $a,b$, do equations.
Continuity at 0: $ae^0+b=\sin0+3$. Slope: left $ae^x$ at 0, right $\frac{d}{dx}(\sin2x)$ at 0.
Slope equation se $a$ nikalo — $\sin 2x$ ka derivative chain rule se $2\cos2x$ hai, 2 mat bhoolo. Phir continuity equation me daalo.
calc-differentiability-10: $\max(x,x^2)$ ka graph jahan dono curves cross karte hain wahan switch karta hai. Wahan slopes alag hon to corner banega.
Crossing points: $x^2=x$ solve karo. Har point par left aur right wale piece ka slope ($1$ ya $2x$) compare karo.
$x^2=x\Rightarrow x(x-1)=0$. Pehle point par slopes $2x$ aur $1$ compare karo, phir doosre par. Trap: sirf ek crossing check karna.
calc-derivative-rules-06: Bahar power 5, andar $2x+1$ — ye chain rule ka case hai.
Andar ka derivative 2 hai — use multiply karna mat bhoolo. Phir $x=0$ daalo, $(2\cdot0+1)^4=1$.
calc-derivative-rules-07: $\frac{x}{e^x}$ ko $xe^{-x}$ likh sakte ho — quotient ki jagah product rule easy padega.
Product rule: $(uv)'=u'v+uv'$ with $u=x$, $v=e^{-x}$, aur $v'=-e^{-x}$ (chain rule se minus).
$u'v=e^{-x}$, $uv'=x\cdot(-e^{-x})$. Ab $e^{-x}$ common nikalo. Trap: $e^{-x}$ ka derivative $+e^{-x}$ likhna.
calc-derivative-rules-08: $x^x$ me base aur exponent dono variable — na power rule chalega na exponential rule akela. Log le lo.
$\ln f=x\ln x$. Dono side differentiate: $\frac{f'}{f}=\ln x+x\cdot\frac1x$.
$f'(x)=x^x(\ln x+1)$. Ab $x=2$ daalo: $2^2=4$ aur $\ln2\approx0.693$. Trap: sirf $x\cdot x^{x-1}$ ya sirf $x^x\ln x$ lena.
calc-derivative-rules-09: Dasvaan derivative haath se nahi — pehle 2–3 derivatives nikal ke pattern dekho.
$f'=e^x+xe^x=(x+1)e^x$. Ab $f''$ nikalo — wo bhi $(x+c)e^x$ form me aayega; $c$ ka pattern dekho.
$f''=e^x+(x+1)e^x$. Pattern ko $n=10$ tak le jao aur $x=0$ daalo. Trap: off-by-one ya $10!$ se multiply karke coefficient bhool jaana.
calc-derivative-rules-10: Char alag derivatives — har ek ko chain/power rule se khud nikal ke given answer se milao.
$(\cos x)'=-\sin x$ — sign dhyan se. $x^{-2}$ ka derivative: power aage aati hai aur exponent 1 kam hota hai, $-2-1$.
calc-taylor-06: $\frac{1}{1+2x}$ geometric series jaisa dikhta hai: $\frac{1}{1-u}$. Bas $u$ kya hai, sign ke saath, wo pehchano.
$x^3$ wala term $u^3=(-2x)^3$ hai — minus aur 2 dono ka cube hoga. Trap: $e^x$ ki tarah $3!$ se divide karna; geometric me factorial nahi hota.
calc-taylor-07: $\sin 2x$ ka series $\sin u$ me $u=2x$ rakh ke milta hai. $x^5$ wala term $u^5$ se aayega.
$\sin u=u-\frac{u^3}{3!}+\frac{u^5}{5!}-\dots$ — $u^5$ term ka sign aur $5!=120$ note karo.
$u^5=(2x)^5=2^5x^5$, to coefficient $\frac{2^5}{120}$. Trap: $2^5$ bhool jaana, ya $u^5$ term ko negative le lena.
calc-taylor-08: Ye do series ka product hai: $e^x$ aur $\frac{1}{1-x}$. $x^3$ ka coefficient har pair se aata hai jinki powers ka sum 3 ho.
Pairs: $(k,m)=(0,3),(1,2),(2,1),(3,0)$ — chaaron add karo. Trap: sirf ek pair lena ya $k=3$ wala chhod dena.
calc-taylor-09: Expansion point $a=2$ hai, 0 nahi. Coefficient $(x-2)^3$ ka chahiye.
$e^x$ ka har derivative $e^x$ hi hai, to $f'''(2)$ seedha likh lo; phir $3!$ se divide karo. Trap: Maclaurin wala $\frac1{3!}$ hi likh dena.
calc-taylor-10: $\cos x$ ka Maclaurin series likho, phir har option alag check karo — kuch coefficient ke baare me hain, kuch derivative ke.
Derivative wale options me $n!$ se multiply karo, coefficient se confuse mat karo. $\cos 2x$ me $u=2x$ — $u^4=(2x)^4$, 2 ka bhi power lagega.
calc-series-sums-06: Har term pichhle ka $\frac13$ — geometric series. Dhyan do sum $n=1$ se shuru hai.
Formula: sum $=\frac{\text{pehla term}}{1-r}$. Yahan $r=\frac13$ aur pehla term $n=1$ par $\frac{5}{3}$.
$1-r=\frac23$. Ab pehle term ko isse divide karo. Trap: pehla term 5 lena — wo $n=0$ ka term hai, jo yahan nahi hai.
calc-series-sums-07: Ratio $r=-\frac12$ — negative hai, lekin $|r|<1$. Sum $n=0$ se shuru hai.
$1-(-\frac12)=1+\frac12$ — minus-minus plus. Ab 1 ko isse divide karo. Trap: minus sign ignore karke $r=\frac12$ le lena.
calc-series-sums-08: Denominator do factors ka product hai jo 2 se differ karte hain — telescoping ke liye partial fractions banao.
$\frac{1}{(2n-1)(2n+1)}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2n-1}-\frac{1}{2n+1}\right)$ — factor $\frac12$ isliye ki dono denominators ka difference 2 hai.
Terms likho: $(1-\frac13)+(\frac13-\frac15)+\dots$ — beech wale cancel. Bacha hua pehla term aur $\frac12$ factor yaad rakho.
calc-series-sums-09: Terms $\frac{n^2}{2^n}$ — $n^2$ badhta hai par $2^n$ bahut tez, to converge. Ye $\sum n^2x^n$ ka case hai, $x=\frac12$.
Formula: $\sum_{n\ge1}n^2x^n=\frac{x(1+x)}{(1-x)^3}$ (yeh $\sum nx^n$ ko differentiate karke $x$ se multiply karne se aata hai).
$x=\frac12$: upar $\frac12\cdot\frac32$, neeche $(\frac12)^3$. Trap: $\sum nx^n$ wala formula laga dena ya $(1+x)$ factor chhodna.
calc-series-sums-10: Har series ke liye ek test chuno: p-series, n-th term test, ya comparison. Terms $\to0$ hona akela kaafi nahi.
p-series $\sum\frac1{n^p}$ converge iff $p>1$. $(-1)^n$ ke terms 0 ki taraf jaate hain? $\frac{n}{n^3+1}$ bade $n$ par kis $\frac{1}{n^p}$ jaisa hai?
$\frac1{\sqrt n}$ me $p=\frac12$; $\frac{n}{n^3+1}\approx\frac{n}{n^3}$. Trap: $(-1)^n$ ke partial sums bounded hain, isliye converge maan lena.
